text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Developments on Palestinian and Syrian peace tracks to top Clinton-Netanyahu talks in Washington.
- Media production city celebrates Eid with the public.
- Final stages of implementation of system that allows immediate refund of cutoms and tax paid on 2,000 kinds of imported goods used in manufacturing of exported items.
- World Bank for Development and Construction gives $445 million for large irrigation projects south of the valley and in Sinai.
- Ministerial committee to discuss in next meeting plans to sell off public sector's share in 65 industrial companies.
- Albright: The United States will continue to support the peace process and to give aid to Egypt and Israel.
- Provinicial investment offices have received 4,901 project proposals, says local administration minister.

- Television and Radio Union to announce within days how it wants to establish media production company. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said union to contribute 40-45 percent of funds for company, investors and private sector to hold 30-35 percent of shares and that remaining shares will be sold to the public.
- Meeting headed by Suzanne Mubarak to discuss development of Helwan.
- EgyptAir chief gives report to Ganzouri on delays in return flights from Saudi Arabia of Egyptian pilgrims.
- Sugar, flour and ghee prices fall.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Ebeid says privatisation of pharmaceutical companies will not push medicine prices up.
- Supply Minister says bread mixed with corn will gradually replace current unmixed bread within five years.
- Parliament to discuss in its current round draft labour law which is expected to be in action by July.
- Egyptian petrol to be lead-free by June, Oil Ministry says.
